items.question: Which number is the odd one out: 5, 7, 9, 11?
items.explanation: Step 1: All four are odd numbers, so look deeper. Step 2: 5, 7 and 11 are prime — only 1 and the number itself divide them. Step 3: 9 = 3 × 3 is not prime, so 9 is the odd one out.
items.source: R.S. Aggarwal, A Modern Approach to Verbal & Non-Verbal Reasoning

items.question: If you walk 3 km north and then 3 km south, you end up where you started.
items.explanation: Step 1: North and south are opposite directions. Step 2: The 3 km south cancels the 3 km north. Step 3: So you are back at the start, even though you walked 6 km in total.
items.source: R.S. Aggarwal, A Modern Approach to Verbal & Non-Verbal Reasoning

items.question: A clock shows exactly 3:00. What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand?
items.explanation: Step 1: A full circle is 360°, and the clock has 12 hour marks, so each mark is 360 ÷ 12 = 30°. Step 2: At 3:00 the hands are 3 marks apart. Step 3: 3 × 30° = 90°, a right angle.
items.source: R.S. Aggarwal, A Modern Approach to Verbal & Non-Verbal Reasoning

items.fact: In any group of 13 people, at least two of them were born in the same month.
items.explanation: Step 1: There are only 12 months. Step 2: Even if the first 12 people all have different months, the 13th person must share a month with someone. Step 3: This idea is called the pigeonhole principle.

items.question: 'Some cats are black. All black things are dark.' Which statement must be true?
items.explanation: Step 1: Only some cats are black, so we know nothing about all cats. Step 2: The black cats are black things, and all black things are dark. Step 3: So those cats are dark — some cats are dark.
items.source: R.S. Aggarwal, A Modern Approach to Verbal & Non-Verbal Reasoning
